title: Continuous presentation matrices and pulled-back coefficient realization
statement: Let E be a normed field, V a scheme, R an abelian ring sheaf and e an invertible morphism from R to the continuous-function coefficient sheaf. For a map f:R^m to R^n define its n by m matrix of global continuous functions by conjugating each regular-module component by e and evaluating it at 1 on the terminal site object. For totally disconnected E and g:V to X define the pulled-back coefficient realization as the canonical condensed coefficient pullback morphism followed by the unique continuous-function realization on V; it is an invertible monoid morphism.

proof.text: Define each component by the corresponding biproduct inclusion, f, and projection. Conjugate by e and evaluate at one.

Construct the condensed coefficient pullback morphism followed by the continuous realization. Prove that this displayed composite uniquely specifies a morphism by equality to it. Define the pullback realization by this proved unique specification, and expose the equality as condensedFieldPullbackRealization_eq. Rewrite by this equation to prove invertibility and monoid compatibility from the original composite. Choosing from an equality to the explicit construction does not change the morphism; it prevents uncontrolled reduction through inverse image in concrete evaluation.
